speed_hint_fast: High concurrency, short timeout: quickest, but may miss slow/filtered ports.
speed_hint_normal: Balanced default, good for most targets.
speed_hint_cautious: Low concurrency, longer timeout: gentler on the target and its rate limits.
empty_description: Set a target above and click Start scan.
guide_intro: An nmap-style TCP connect scanner: it attempts a real handshake on each port and reports what came back. No raw sockets / SYN scan (that needs root), so this is the equivalent of <0>nmap -sT</0>.
guide_step1_body: A hostname or IP. <0>scanme.nmap.org</0> is the Nmap project's own public test target if you want to try it out safely.
guide_step2_body: <0>Top 100 / Top 1000</0> scan the most commonly open TCP ports (ranked by real-world frequency, from nmap's own service database): fast and usually enough. <1>Custom range</1> takes a spec like <2>{{spec}}</2> for anything else, up to the full 1-65535 range.
guide_step3_body: <0>Fast</0> pushes concurrency up and the timeout down: quickest, but can misread a slow/rate-limited target as filtered. <1>Cautious</1> does the opposite: fewer parallel connections, longer timeout, easier on a target that rate-limits or has a sensitive firewall. <2>Normal</2> is a balanced default.
guide_step4_title: Click "Start scan" and watch it stream in
guide_step4_body: Every port is probed concurrently, and results land in the table as they come back. "Stop" cancels a running scan at any point, handy for a big custom range you want to cut short.
guide_step5_body: <0>open</0>: the handshake succeeded; a service is listening. <1>closed</1>: the host answered but refused the connection; nothing's there. <2>filtered</2>: no response at all before the timeout, usually a firewall silently dropping the packets.
guide_step6_body: <0>Service</0> is the port's well-known name (e.g. 22 → ssh), not a live detection. <1>Banner</1> is whatever bytes the open port sent back unprompted in the first moment after connecting: many services (SSH, FTP, SMTP) announce themselves this way; others (plain HTTP) stay silent until asked, so it's often empty.
guide_footer_note: This makes real TCP connections to every port scanned. Only use it against hosts you're authorized to test.
